newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks stage broad rally, Dow surges 104 pts.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks stage broad rally, Dow surges 104 pts.

text.p: U.S. blue chips surged to yet another record high on Tuesday in a broad display of market confidence over the outlook for the economy and second quarter earnings.

The Dow industrials soared 104 points to close unofficially at 7962. The closing level marked the Dow's thirtieth record high for the year and left the blue chip average well within striking distance of the 8000 mark.
"Eight thousand is a foregone conclusion at this point," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd.
"We've been hemming and hawing just below 8000 and the next time we make a move we'll probably blast right through," he said.
Cyclical stocks paced the advance among blue chips, with International Paper Co jumping 4-11/16 to 56 after reporting second quarter operating earnings that beat Wall Street estimates.
IP became the second Dow component to beat estimates in as many days, following Monday's release of stronger than expected earnings from Aluminum Co of America, another economically sensitive issue.

Investors quickly seized on the good news, bidding up IP and other cyclicals after largely shunning the group earlier this year over concerns over the potential economic impact of interest rate increases by the Federal Reserve.
With rate fears now mostly out of the picture, analysts said economically sensitive stocks were back in favor.

"Cyclicals had really underperformed year-to-date and from a valuation standpoint many of them were attractive compared to the Cokes and GEs," said Jack Shaughnessy, director of research at Advest. "We're starting to see money rotate back to them now."
Motorola climbed 2-7/16 to a year-high of 82-13/16 ahead of the release of its earnings, expected after the close.

Among other individual issues, Procter & Gamble Co jumped 5-7/8 to 150. The company announced a two-for-one stock split, raised its quarterly dividend by 12 percent and said it planned to spend a total of about $1 billion on share buybacks over fiscal 1997 and 1998.
There were market soft spots. Several small networking software companies tumbled after announcing their second quarter results would fail to match expectations.

The companies included the four top percentage decliners on Nasdaq, each of which fell more than 30 percent. XcelleNet Inc tumbled five to 8-7/8, Wall Data Inc slid 9-7/8 to 17-7/8, Segue Software Inc fell 4-7/16 to 8-11/16 and Dataworks Corp fell 6-1/4 to 13-1/4.
The Nasdaq Composite rose 14.36 points to 1485.10 and the S&P 500 index rose 6.55 points to 918.75, both records.
